title: M3 — tool modules
objective: Build a small declarative tool/action/processing interface and implement the pixel editor and existing transforms through it, preserving saved history.
context_summary: Starts from the implemented pixel/transform editor with persistent history. Linked modules are sufficient; external binary loading is later work. Design: docs/design/modules-and-api.md.

acceptance_criteria: Use the proven history/pixel/transform editor as the named input and keep core transactions/history independent of the descriptor representation.
Define module/effect identity, schemas, units/defaults/ranges, validation/errors, state/discovery, processing and resource/cancellation requirements.
Define semantic controls and optional canvas interactions whose presentation is chosen by the GUI; every control maps to a declared API action.
Review the pixel and transform tools against the contract; persisted operations can be identified and preserved if a provider is unavailable.

steps: Map existing action inputs and UI controls to one descriptor and identify host/module ownership.
Check that an independent headless caller needs no UI state and modules need no database writes.
expected_results: Review the pixel and transform tools against the contract; persisted operations can be identified and preserved if a provider is unavailable.

acceptance_criteria: Register linked providers with cheap metadata discovery, duplicate-ID rejection and lazy resources.
Dispatch UI/API actions through module validation into host-owned transactions/history; rendering resolves immutable effect payloads through registered processors.
Keep unknown effect payloads and snapshots intact with explicit unavailable-effect results; never silently render/export a reduced stack.
Tests reject malformed descriptors, missing handlers, unsupported payloads and failed actions without authoritative state mutation.

steps: Exercise registry/discovery and processor resolution with small test providers.
Check schema/action/control completeness and shared transaction behavior headlessly.
expected_results: Tests reject malformed descriptors, missing handlers, unsupported payloads and failed actions without authoritative state mutation.

acceptance_criteria: Move pixel parameters, schemas, validation and processing into a module using the host interface.
Describe x/y/RGB/Apply controls and any canvas picker binding declaratively, preserving the original durable effect ID and payload meaning.
Load pre-module saved catalogs and render their history unchanged; any required internal conversion must preserve data and be explicitly tested.
Module actions create the same layers/history and exact pixels as the original built-in proof through both direct and external API calls.

steps: Replay saved pixel fixtures and compare pre/post-module stack and pixel results.
Test invalid channels/coordinates, no-ops, retries and missing-provider recovery.
expected_results: Module actions create the same layers/history and exact pixels as the original built-in proof through both direct and external API calls.

acceptance_criteria: Adapt the basic-transform handlers to the same tool interface while preserving operation IDs, coordinates and layer evaluation order.
Provide action/control descriptors for rotations and both reflections with no alternate history implementation.
Existing pixel/transform catalogs retain stable IDs, complete snapshots and undo/restore behavior across the module integration.
Disabled/missing test providers preserve effects and visibly report rendering limitations; valid providers restore evaluation without rewriting history.

steps: Compare every saved transform/pixel fixture before and after registration changes.
Test registry failures and missing providers across current and historical snapshot rendering.
expected_results: Disabled/missing test providers preserve effects and visibly report rendering limitations; valid providers restore evaluation without rewriting history.
